alt: DMHC Response to Grievance regarding L.A. Care Health Plan and transportation denials (June 26, 2026) - Page 1. The letter acknowledges the complaint about being trapped on hold and denied transport, stating that L.A. Care referred the concerns to its own quality assurance program.
full_text: DEPARTMENT OF Managed Health Care June 26, 2026 NICOLAS HERNANDEZ CA 9 Patient: Nicolas Hernandez DMHC#: [REDACTED]44 Health Plan: Local Initiative Health Authority for L.A. County (L.A. Care Health Plan) Dear Nicolas Hernandez: Thank you for sending your Independent Medical Review (IMR)/Complaint Form to the Department of Managed Health Care (Department). The Department reviewed your complaint in which you expressed dissatisfaction with your experience with L.A. Care Health Plan. In your complaint, you stated that you attempted to utilize L.A. Care's mandated non-emergency medical transportation benefits to travel to the pharmacy to pick up critical, time-sensitive prescription medications. However, the health plan's transportation phone lines subjected you to excessive, unlawful hold times, effectively denying you timely access to covered prescription services. Our review included your complaint documents, health plan response, and Evidence of Coverage (health plan contract). Quality Concerns For the quality concerns in your complaint, L.A. Care Health Plan referred your concerns to L.A. Care Health Plan's quality assurance program for further investigation. This means L.A. Care Health Plan will evaluate the quality of your experience. California law requires health plans to identify and correct any quality problems. While the Department monitors health plan quality assurance programs to make sure they are addressing quality concerns, the Department cannot provide the specific outcome of the quality review in relation to your complaint. Please be advised, the Department and/or health plans are not responsible for the professional practice of individual doctors, nurses, and other providers. If you would like to pursue a complaint against a specific provider, please contact the agency listed below. To file a complaint against a specific non-emergency medical transportation provider, you may contact the California Department of Health Care Services at: Protecting the Health Care Rights of More Than 30.2 Million Californians Contact the DMHC Help Center at 1-888-466-2219 or www.DMHC.ca.gov
summary: Page 1 of the official DMHC response dated June 26, 2026, confirming receipt of the complaint regarding L.A. Care's non-emergency medical transportation access failures. The DMHC notes that L.A. Care referred the quality concerns to its own internal quality assurance program for evaluation.
